title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 25 (Agreement without consideration, void, unless it is in writing and registered, or is a promise to compensate for something done, or is a promise to pay a debt barred by limitation law)

content.overview: Section 25 provides that an agreement made without consideration is void, unless — (1) it is expressed in writing and registered under the law for the time being in force for the registration of documents, and is made on account of natural love and affection between parties standing in a near relation to each other; or (2) it is a promise to compensate, wholly or in part, a person who has already voluntarily done something for the promisor, or something which the promisor was legally compellable to do; or (3) it is a promise, made in writing and signed by the person to be charged therewith, or by his agent generally or specially authorised in that behalf, to pay wholly or in part a debt of which the creditor might have enforced payment but for the law for the limitation of suits. Explanation 1: Nothing in this section shall affect the validity, as between the donor and donee, of any gift actually made. Explanation 2: An agreement to which the consent of the promisor is freely given is not void merely because the consideration is inadequate; but the inadequacy of the consideration may be taken into account by the Court in determining the question whether the consent of the promisor was freely given.
content.glance: No consideration → void, except: (1) written+registered near-relation natural love and affection; (2) promise to compensate past voluntary act; (3) written signed promise to pay time-barred debt; gift validity saved; inadequacy alone does not void.
content.study: Default: agreement without consideration is void. Three exceptions: (1) writing and registration, natural love and affection, near relation; (2) promise to compensate for something already voluntarily done for the promisor or which the promisor was legally compellable to do; (3) written and signed promise to pay a time-barred debt. Completed gifts between donor and donee are not affected. Inadequacy of consideration alone does not void if consent is free, but may be relevant to freeness of consent. Current-law framing: establish absence of consideration; test each exception; apply explanations.

sections.heading: Default rule
sections.body: Agreement made without consideration is void.

sections.heading: Exception — natural love and affection
sections.body: Writing + registration + natural love and affection + near relation.

sections.heading: Exception — past voluntary act
sections.body: Promise to compensate for something already voluntarily done for the promisor, or which the promisor was legally compellable to do.

sections.heading: Exception — time-barred debt
sections.body: Written and signed promise to pay wholly or in part a debt barred by limitation.

sections.heading: Gift and inadequacy
sections.body: Completed gift validity saved; inadequacy alone does not void if consent free.

provisions.title: Agreement without consideration, void, unless it is in writing and registered, or is a promise to compensate for something done, or is a promise to pay a debt barred by limitation law

examples.title: Time-barred debt
examples.body: A signs a written promise to pay a debt barred by limitation. The promise is enforceable under s. 25(3) without fresh consideration.

hypotheticals.question: Is every gift void for want of consideration?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Explanation 1 saves the validity of a gift actually made as between donor and donee.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-25
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: No agreement without consideration can ever be enforced.
misconceptions.correction: Section 25 has three statutory exceptions and saves completed gifts.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 25 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Establish absence of consideration. II. Test each of the three exceptions. III. Apply gift and inadequacy explanations. IV. Conclude.

examTips: List the three exceptions with all conditions.
